135.matn: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from Hammām ibn Munabbih: that he heard Abū Huraira say: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The prayer of one who has broken his purification is not accepted until he performs ablution.” A man from Ḥaḍramawt said: What is ḥadath, O Abū Huraira? He said: Silent or audible passing of wind.
135.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “No prayer is accepted without purification”. The Prophet ﷺ ties acceptance of the prayer to ablution after ḥadath has occurred. The explanation of what ḥadath is is Abū Huraira’s answer to the questioner from Ḥaḍramawt, not a prophetic saying in this entry.

136.matn: Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to us, from Khālid, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Hilāl, from Nuʿaym al-Mujmir, he said: “I went up with Abū Huraira onto the roof of the mosque, and he performed ablution. Then he said: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: My community will be called on the Day of Resurrection with shining foreheads and limbs from the traces of ablution. So whoever among you can lengthen his blaze (al-ghurra), let him do so.”
136.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on the virtue of ablution and those with shining foreheads and limbs. The radiance is traced to the marks of ablution. The encouragement to lengthen the ghurra is in the wording of this report; a closer definition of how far that goes is not added here.

137.matn: ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, from his uncle: “that he complained to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of the man to whom it seems that he finds the thing in the prayer. He said: He should not step away – or: he should not turn aside – until he hears a sound or finds a smell.”
137.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter that one does not repeat ablution out of doubt until certain. Mere imagination does not break the prayer; certainty here comes by hearing or smelling. The uncertainty “step away or turn aside” is preserved. The uncle remains unnamed, as in the wording.

138.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, he said: Kurayb informed me, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept until he snored, then prayed. And he sometimes said: He lay down until he snored, then rose and prayed.” Then Sufyān narrated it to us time after time, from ʿAmr, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I spent the night at my aunt Maymūna’s. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose in the night. When part of the night had passed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose, performed a light ablution from a hanging water-skin – ʿAmr used to describe it as light and little – and stood to pray. I performed an ablution similar to his, then came and stood at his left – and Sufyān sometimes said: at his north side – so he turned me and put me at his right. Then he prayed as long as Allah willed, then lay down and slept until he snored. Then the caller came and announced the prayer to him. He rose with him to the prayer, prayed, and did not perform (a fresh) ablution. We said to ʿAmr: People say: The eye of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sleeps, and his heart does not sleep. ʿAmr said: I heard ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr say: The dreams of the prophets are revelation. Then he recited: “I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you.”
138.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: The same chapter of doubt and certainty in ablution. The report shows that the Prophet ﷺ slept until he snored and then prayed without a fresh ablution. The uncertainties “slept or lay down” and “left or north side” are preserved, as is ʿAmr’s description of the light ablution. The remark that the prophets’ hearts do not sleep stands as a saying “of the people”; ʿAmr supports it with ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr’s word that the prophets’ dreams are revelation, and with the well-known verse. That is marked as a scholar’s note, not a prophetic saying in this chain.

139.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Maslama narrated to us, from Mālik, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqba, from Kurayb, the client of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Usāma ibn Zayd: that he heard him say: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, moved on from ʿArafa until, when he was at the mountain pass, he dismounted and urinated, then performed ablution and did not do it thoroughly. I said: The prayer, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The prayer is ahead of you. Then he mounted; when he came to al-Muzdalifa he dismounted, performed ablution and did it thoroughly. Then the prayer was established, he prayed the sunset prayer, then each man made his camel kneel at his stopping place, then the night prayer was established and he prayed, and he prayed nothing between them.”
139.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Performing ablution thoroughly”. At the pass he performs an ablution that is not thorough; the prayer is “ahead of you”, at al-Muzdalifa. There he performs it thoroughly and joins the sunset and night prayers with no prayer between them. The difference between the two ablutions is in the text itself.

140.matn: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm narrated to us, he said: Abū Salama al-Khuzāʿī Manṣūr ibn Salama informed us, he said: Ibn Bilāl, meaning Sulaymān, informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “that he performed ablution and washed his face: he took a handful of water and with it rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, then took a handful of water and did like this with it, adding it to his other hand, and washed his face with both, then took a handful of water and washed his right hand with it, then took a handful of water and washed his left hand with it, then wiped his head, then took a handful of water and poured it over his right foot until he had washed it, then took another handful and washed his foot with it, meaning the left. Then he said: Thus I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.”
140.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Washing the face with both hands from a single handful”. Ibn ʿAbbās demonstrates the ablution. Rinsing the mouth and the nose is from one handful; the face is washed with both hands from a handful added to the other. The gloss “meaning the left” is an explanation by the narrator.

141.matn: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdallāh narrated to us, he said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Kurayb, from Ibn ʿAbbās, raising it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “If one of you, when he comes to his wife, were to say: In the name of Allah, O Allah, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You have provided us, and then a child were decreed between them, it would not harm him.”
141.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Saying Allah’s name in every state and at intercourse”. The formula is at the start of intercourse; the protection concerns the child, if one is granted. The wording does not specify the harm more closely, and that is not supplied here.

142.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb, he said: I heard Anas say: “When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the toilet, he said: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from foulness and the foul ones (al-khubuth wa-l-khabāʾith).” Ibn ʿArʿara corroborated him (in narrating) from Shuʿba. Ghundar said, from Shuʿba: when he came to the toilet. Mūsā said, from Ḥammād: when he entered. Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us: when he wanted to enter.
142.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “What to say on entering the toilet”. The plea for refuge is constant; the wordings “entered, came, went in, wanted to enter” are preserved as narrator variants. Ibn ʿArʿara’s following is marked as a supporting path.

143.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: Warqāʾ narrated to us, from ʿUbaydallāh ibn Abī Yazīd, from Ibn ʿAbbās: “that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the toilet, and I placed water for ablution for him. He said: Who put this here? He was told. Then he said: O Allah, grant him understanding in the religion.”
143.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “Placing water at the toilet”. Ibn ʿAbbās sets out the water; the supplication for understanding in the religion is for him. Who gave the report remains unnamed in the wording.

144.matn: Ādam narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, he said: al-Zuhrī narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī, from Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you comes to relieve himself, let him not face the qibla nor turn his back to it; face east or west.”
144.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter on not facing the qibla when relieving oneself, except in a building. The instruction “east or west” fits the situation of Medina, where the qibla is to the south; an extension to other bearings is not fixed here. The chapter itself names the exception behind a wall; this entry does not spell it out.

145.matn: ʿAbdallāh ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, he said: Mālik informed us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥibbān, from his uncle Wāsiʿ ibn Ḥibbān, from ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar: “that he used to say: People say: When you sit for your need, do not face the qibla or the Sacred House (Bayt al-Maqdis). ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿUmar said: I went up one day onto the roof of a house of ours and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on two bricks, facing the Sacred House, for his need. And he said: Perhaps you are of those who pray on their hips? I said: I do not know, by Allah.” Mālik said: He means the one who prays and does not rise from the ground, who prostrates while stuck to the earth.
145.sharh: AI summary, with no invented page number: Al-Bukhārī places the hadith under the chapter “One who relieved himself squatting on two bricks”. Ibn ʿUmar counters the general claim with what he himself saw: the Prophet ﷺ with his back to the qibla and his face toward the Sacred House, in a built area. The question about “praying on the hips” is Ibn ʿUmar’s address to his interlocutor, not a prophetic saying. Mālik’s explanation of that posture is marked as a scholar’s note.
